segments.en: Welcome back to another podcast here at EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 欢迎回到 Englishpod 的另一个播客。

segments.en: And today we're looking at another one of our lessons for English of the past decades.
segments.zh: 今天，我们正在研究过去几十年英语的另一堂课。

segments.en: Well, you know, the 1990s is a little easier for most of us to remember.
segments.zh: 好吧，你知道，1990 年代对我们大多数人来说更容易记住。

segments.en: Yeah, I guess it's a little bit more recent.
segments.zh: 是的，我想这离现在更近一些。

segments.en: We're going to be looking at a lot of language that is still used today.
segments.zh: 我们将研究许多今天仍在使用的语言。

segments.en: Most of these words and phrases are still used today.
segments.zh: 这些单词和短语中的大多数至今仍在使用。

segments.en: So they're going to be very useful.
And you're going to sound a lot more native.
A lot cooler as well, huh?
So before we get started with this lesson, why don't we take a look at vocabulary preview?
segments.zh: 所以在我们开始本课程之前，我们为什么不看看词汇预览呢？

segments.en: We have two words we're going to hear in the dialogue.
segments.zh: 我们将在对话中听到两个词。

segments.en: Now the first one is a mall.
All right, so a mall is basically short for shopping mall.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以商场基本上是购物中心的缩写。

segments.en: And a shopping mall is a big building with many stores inside.
segments.zh: 购物中心是一座大楼，里面有很多商店。

segments.en: So it's like a shopping center.
segments.zh: 所以它就像一个购物中心。

segments.en: And our last word for vocabulary preview is gang.
segments.zh: 我们的词汇预览的最后一个词是帮派。

segments.en: Okay, so a gang is a group of people, right?
segments.zh: 好吧，一个团伙是一群人，对吧？

segments.en: Yeah, it's a group of people.
You can call your friends the gang.
segments.zh: 你可以称你的朋友为团伙。

segments.en: We're going to go out with the gang tonight.
segments.zh: 今晚我们要和帮派出去。

segments.en: And we sometimes hear this word and it has a negative meaning, right?
segments.zh: 我们有时会听到这个词，它有负面的含义，对吧？

segments.en: Yeah, so people who fight and deal drugs and all that sort of stuff.
segments.zh: 是的，所以那些打架和交易毒品之类的人。

segments.en: So it can have a negative and a positive meaning, but it just depends on how you use it.
segments.zh: 所以它可以有负面和积极的含义，但这取决于你如何使用它。

segments.en: Yeah, but in the dialogue we'll hear it with a positive meaning.
segments.zh: 是的，但在对话中，我们会以积极的含义听到它。

segments.en: So that's all the words we have for vocabulary preview.
segments.zh: 这就是我们对词汇预览的所有词。

segments.en: Let's listen to this cool and hip dialogue from the 1990s and we'll come back later and explain some words.
segments.zh: 让我们听听 1990 年代酷炫时尚的对话，我们稍后会回来解释一些单词。

segments.en: Just went to the mall and picked up some junk.
segments.zh: 刚去商场买了些杂七杂八的东西。

segments.en: You are going to be getting mad props from the gang, man.
segments.zh: 哥们，那帮朋友肯定会对你赞不绝口的。

segments.en: Anyways, have you seen Betty lately?
segments.zh: 不管怎样，你最近见过贝蒂吗？

segments.en: That girl started tripping because I went to the movies with Veronica the other day.
segments.zh: 前几天我和维罗妮卡去看电影，那女孩就大发脾气。

segments.en: I was like, look, you knew how I was before you got with me.
segments.zh: 我就说，听着，你跟我在一起之前就知道我是什么样的人。

segments.en: You are such a player, man.
segments.zh: 哥们，你真是个花花公子。

segments.en: You look like you just saw a ghost.
segments.zh: 你看起来就像刚刚看到了一个鬼。

segments.en: I got an F in English class.
segments.zh: 我英语得了个 F，不及格。

segments.en: You need to lay off the books for a while and have some fun.
segments.zh: 你得暂时放下书本，出去玩玩。

segments.en: My dad is going to go postal when he finds out about this.
segments.zh: 我爸要是知道了，肯定会大发雷霆。

segments.en: I'm going to open the can of whoop ass on you if you don't come with me right now.
segments.zh: 你现在要是不跟我走，我就揍你一顿。

segments.en: Well, it sounds like this guy's got some problems at school, huh?
segments.zh: 好吧，听起来这家伙在学校有一些问题，对吧？

segments.en: Yeah, he got an F on his paper, but you always can count on your friends to try and cheer you up by doing something.
segments.zh: 是的，他的考卷上得了个 F，但你总可以指望朋友想点办法逗你开心。

segments.en: Yeah, but they use some really great phrases and vocabulary words, so why don't we look at those now in Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 是的，但他们用了一些非常棒的短语和词汇，所以我们现在就去语言要点里看看这些吧。

segments.en: All right, on Language Takeaway we're going to be looking at five words and well, let's start with the first one.
segments.zh: 好吧，在语言要点方面，我们将看五个单词，好吧，让我们从第一个开始。

segments.en: So the guy was talking about his really cool new shoes, his new Adidas, right?
segments.zh: 所以这家伙在谈论他非常酷的新鞋，他的新阿迪达斯，对吧？

segments.en: And his friend said, those are dope.
Okay, so it's pretty easy to understand when something is dope.
segments.zh: 好的，所以当某些东西是 DOPE 时，很容易理解。

segments.en: So his friend said, those are dope.
segments.zh: 所以他的朋友说，那些真酷。

segments.en: And he said, you're going to be getting mad props from the gang.
segments.zh: 他说，那帮朋友肯定会对你大加赞赏。

segments.en: We can divide this word in two.
segments.zh: 我们可以把这个词一分为二。

segments.en: So let's take a look at the first part, mad.
segments.zh: 所以让我们来看看第一部分，疯狂。

segments.en: So we understand that mad is angry, right?
segments.zh: 所以我们知道 MAD 很生气，对吧？

segments.en: Yeah, but it can also mean a lot, right?
segments.zh: 是的，但它也可能意味着很多，对吧？

segments.en: So if I say, you have mad skills.
segments.zh: 所以如果我说，你技能超强。

segments.en: Or you can say, she has a mad amount of shoes.
segments.zh: 或者你可以说，她有大量的鞋子。

segments.en: So he's going to get mad props.
segments.zh: 所以他会赢得大家的称赞。

segments.en: Now props is like respect or compliments.
segments.zh: 这里的 props 是指尊重或赞美。

segments.en: So his shoes are so cool that he's going to get a lot of respect or a lot of compliments from his friends.
segments.zh: 所以他的鞋子太酷了，他会得到很多尊重或朋友的赞美。

segments.en: So they started talking about girls and he mentioned that this girl started tripping.
segments.zh: 所以他们开始聊女孩，他提到那个女孩开始发飙了。
正如你注意到的，它读作 trippin'。

segments.en: It doesn't have the G at the end, which isn't really grammatically correct, but that's kind of the way it's pronounced.
segments.zh: 它没有最后的 G，这在语法上并不正确，但这就是它的发音方式。

segments.en: We would never say the G. Right.
segments.zh: 我们永远不会说 G. 对。
所以如果有人说自己 trippin'。

segments.en: So why don't we listen to a couple of examples of how we could use trippin' for different situations.
segments.zh: 那么，我们为什么不听一些关于如何在不同情况下使用 Trippin' 的例子。

segments.en: Leanne was trippin' because I got dirt on her car.
segments.zh: Leanne 大发脾气，因为我把脏东西弄到了她的车上。

segments.en: Even though I apologized for calling her fat, Jeannie was trippin' all night.
segments.zh: 尽管我为说她胖道了歉，珍妮还是整晚都在发飙。

segments.en: He sent me 43 text messages and called me about 20 times.
segments.zh: 他给我发了 43 条短信，给我打了大约 20 次。

segments.en: That guy is trippin' over me.
Now, moving on to our next word.
segments.zh: 现在，继续我们的下一个词。

segments.en: They wanted to go somewhere and he said, come on, let's bounce.
segments.zh: 他们想去个地方，他说，来吧，我们走。

segments.en: Now, bounce basically means let's leave.
segments.zh: 现在，Bounce 基本上意味着让我们离开。

segments.en: But we might be more familiar with this word as in like a ball, right?
segments.zh: 但我们可能更熟悉这个词，就像一个球一样，对吧？

segments.en: A ball bounces off the floor.
So I guess it's kind of the same.
You kind of bounce off the floor and leave that place.
segments.zh: 你有点从地板上弹下来，然后离开那个地方。

segments.en: Okay, so for our final word.
Now, this guy who got a bad mark on his paper, he was nervous about what his dad would say, right?
segments.zh: 现在，这个考卷上分数很差的人，他很紧张，不知道他爸会怎么说，对吧？

segments.en: Because his dad was going to go postal.
He said, my dad is gonna go postal.
Now, if you go postal, it means you go crazy.
segments.zh: 现在，如果你 go postal，意思是你发疯了。

segments.en: This word comes from the 90s because during a time, it was very common in the United States that postal workers, mailmen, were going a little bit crazy and they started shooting people and delivering some strange packages.
segments.zh: 这个词来自 90 年代，因为在美国，邮政工人、邮递员有点疯狂，他们开始射人并运送一些奇怪的包裹是很常见的。

segments.en: Well, I guess so people who work in the post office maybe don't have the most exciting jobs and that drives them a little crazy.
segments.zh: 好吧，我想在邮局工作的人可能没有最令人兴奋的工作，这让他们有点发疯。

segments.en: But now they have a term named after them.
segments.zh: 但现在他们有一个以他们命名的术语。

segments.en: So why don't we listen to our dialogue for the second time?
segments.zh: 那么我们为什么不第二次听我们的对话呢？

segments.en: We're going to slow it down a little bit and then we'll come back.
segments.zh: 我们要慢一点，然后我们会回来。

segments.en: Just went to the mall and picked up some junk.
segments.zh: 刚去商场买了些杂七杂八的东西。

segments.en: You are going to be getting mad props from the gang, man.
segments.zh: 哥们，那帮朋友肯定会对你赞不绝口的。

segments.en: Anyways, have you seen Betty lately?
segments.zh: 不管怎样，你最近见过贝蒂吗？

segments.en: That girl started tripping because I went to the movies with Veronica the other day.
segments.zh: 前几天我和维罗妮卡去看电影，那女孩就大发脾气。

segments.en: I was like, look, you knew how I was before you got with me.
segments.zh: 我就说，听着，你跟我在一起之前就知道我是什么样的人。

segments.en: You are such a player, man.
segments.zh: 哥们，你真是个花花公子。

segments.en: You look like you just saw a ghost.
segments.zh: 你看起来就像刚刚看到了一个鬼。

segments.en: I got an F in English class.
segments.zh: 我英语得了个 F，不及格。

segments.en: You need to lay off the books for a while and have some fun.
segments.zh: 你得暂时放下书本，出去玩玩。

segments.en: My dad is going to go postal when he finds out about this.
segments.zh: 我爸要是知道了，肯定会大发雷霆。

segments.en: I'm going to open a can of whoop-ass on you if you don't come with me right now.
segments.zh: 你要是现在不跟我走，我就狠狠揍你一顿。

segments.en: Okay, so I think that was a little easier to understand.
segments.zh: 好的，所以我认为这更容易理解。

segments.en: You know, we've got a lot of pretty strange words and phrases, some interesting slang.
segments.zh: 你知道，我们有很多非常奇怪的单词和短语，一些有趣的俚语。

segments.en: Yeah, and I want to take a look at this slang now, so let's get started with Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 是的，我现在想看看这个俚语，所以让我们开始使用流利表达。

segments.en: Okay, so the guy with the new shoes, he asked his friends, have you seen Betty lately, right?
segments.zh: 好吧，那个穿新鞋的人，他问他的朋友们，你最近见过贝蒂，对吧？

segments.en: And his friend replied, don't even go there.
segments.zh: 他的朋友回答说，别提这事。

segments.en: And he said, dude, don't even go there.
So what does he mean when he says, don't even go there?
segments.zh: 那么他说别提这事，是什么意思？

segments.en: He means, don't talk about it.
segments.zh: 他的意思是，不要谈论它。

segments.en: I don't want to talk about it.
So if somebody wants to talk about a topic that you think is sensitive or you don't want to talk about, just say, hey, don't even go there.
segments.zh: 因此，如果有人想聊你觉得敏感、不想谈的话题，你就说，嘿，别提这事。

segments.en: So Marco, what do you think about the new tax law?
segments.zh: 那么马可，您如何看待新的税法？

segments.en: I don't even want to talk about politics.
I think that's a really actually quite helpful phrase to avoid talking about an uncomfortable subject.
segments.zh: 我认为这实际上是一个非常有用的短语，可以避免谈论一个不舒服的话题。

segments.en: So he said, don't even go there.
And he started talking about the girl and she was tripping.
segments.zh: 他开始聊那个女孩，她当时正发飙。

segments.en: And then he said something interesting.
segments.zh: 然后他说了一些有趣的话。

segments.en: He said, I was like, look, you knew how I was before you got with me.
segments.zh: 他说，我就说，听着，你跟我在一起之前就知道我是什么样的人。

segments.en: Yeah, I really like this phrase.
segments.zh: 是的，我真的很喜欢这句话。

segments.en: Now, I want to focus on the first part.
segments.zh: 现在，我想专注于第一部分。

segments.en: Now, you might hear a lot of native English speakers use these three words before they start telling you what they said.
segments.zh: 现在，您可能会听到很多以英语为母语的人在开始告诉您他们所说的内容之前使用这三个词。

segments.en: So it's like saying, I said or I told him.
segments.zh: 所以这就像说，我说或我告诉他。

segments.en: So this actually is really common, especially with people under the age of 30.
segments.zh: 所以这实际上很常见，尤其是对于30岁以下的人。

segments.en: So why don't we hear a few more examples of how it's used now.
segments.zh: 那么我们为什么不听听更多关于它现在如何使用的例子。

segments.en: This guy caused a car accident.

segments.zh: 我当时就说，你这个白痴。

segments.en: You can kill people by driving like that.
And then I was like, I hate you.
And she was all like, I hate you more.
I told the teacher that I didn't finish my homework and he was like, I'll see you after school.
segments.zh: 我告诉老师我没有完成我的作业，他说，放学后见。

segments.en: So if you're telling a story or you're maybe talking to somebody and you want to explain what you said, you can say, I was like, hey, what are you doing?
segments.zh: 所以如果你在讲故事，或者跟人聊天时想转述你说过的话，你可以说，我就说，嘿，你在干嘛？

segments.en: So you can have an entire dialogue based with I was like, she was like, we were like.
segments.zh: 所以你可以用“我就说”“她就说”“我们就说”撑起一整段对话。

segments.en: So I was like, it's super, super useful.
segments.zh: 所以我想，它超级，超级有用。
所以现在我们的下一个词。

segments.en: Now, they saw their friend who got the bad marking in school and the guy said, dude, get over it.
segments.zh: 现在，他们看到在学校得了差评的那个朋友，那家伙说，哥们，别再纠结了。

segments.en: So if somebody tells you to get over it.
segments.zh: 所以如果有人让你别再纠结了。

segments.en: So if somebody is sad because maybe his girlfriend broke up with him, you would say, get over it.
segments.zh: 所以如果有人因为女朋友跟他分手而难过，你会说，别再纠结了。

segments.en: And you commonly use this for when somebody is upset about a small thing, something they shouldn't worry about.
segments.zh: 当有人为一件小事、为不该担心的事心烦时，你通常这么说。

segments.en: Now, why don't we go on to our final word?
segments.zh: 现在，我们为什么不继续我们的最后一句话？

segments.en: At the end of the dialogue, they said, I'm going to open a can of whoop ass.
segments.zh: 在对话结尾，他们说，我要狠狠揍你一顿。

segments.en: So to open a can of whoop ass on somebody.
segments.zh: 所以，to open a can of whoop ass on somebody。

segments.en: To open a can of whoop ass.
So again, let's break this down before we explain it.
segments.zh: 再说一次，让我们在解释之前分解一下。

segments.en: I think we have to take one step back here.
segments.zh: 我认为我们必须在这里退一步。

segments.en: To whoop someone's ass is to beat them up, right?
segments.zh: 揍某人一顿就是把他打趴下，对吧？

segments.en: To punch them and hurt them.
So if I open a can of whoop ass, what does that mean?
segments.zh: 那么，如果我打开一罐 Whoop Ass，那是什么意思？

segments.en: It means you're going to beat them up.
segments.zh: 意思是你要把他揍一顿。

segments.en: So it's just a funny, very informal way of saying like, in this can, I'm going to open it and I'm going to start hitting you or something like that.
segments.zh: 所以这只是一种有趣、非常非正式的说法，比如，在这个罐头里，我要打开它，我将开始打你或类似的东西。

segments.en: Some sort of small man is going to jump out of the can and start hitting you.
segments.zh: 某种小人会从罐子里跳出来开始打你。
但它从来都不是字面的。

segments.en: It's not like you're actually going to beat somebody up.
It's just kind of like a joke.
So some really interesting words and phrases in this dialogue.
segments.zh: 所以在这个对话中有一些非常有趣的单词和短语。

segments.en: I think we should listen to it for the last time and then we'll come back and talk a little bit more about this great decade.
segments.zh: 我认为我们应该最后一次听它，然后我们会回来再谈谈这个伟大的十年。

segments.en: Just went to the mall and picked up some junk.
segments.zh: 刚去商场买了些杂七杂八的东西。

segments.en: You are going to be getting mad props from the gang, man.
segments.zh: 哥们，那帮朋友肯定会对你赞不绝口的。

segments.en: Anyways, have you seen Betty lately?
segments.zh: 不管怎样，你最近见过贝蒂吗？

segments.en: That girl started tripping because I went to the movies with Veronica the other day.
segments.zh: 前几天我和维罗妮卡去看电影，那女孩就大发脾气。

segments.en: I was like, look, you knew how I was before you got with me.
segments.zh: 我就说，听着，你跟我在一起之前就知道我是什么样的人。

segments.en: You are such a player, man.
segments.zh: 哥们，你真是个花花公子。

segments.en: You look like you just saw a ghost.
segments.zh: 你看起来就像刚刚看到了一个鬼。

segments.en: I got an F in English class.
segments.zh: 我英语得了个 F，不及格。

segments.en: You need to lay off the books for a while and have some fun.
segments.zh: 你得暂时放下书本，出去玩玩。

segments.en: My dad is going to go postal when he finds out about this.
segments.zh: 我爸要是知道了，肯定会大发雷霆。

segments.en: I'm going to open a can of whoop-ass on you if you don't come with me right now.
segments.zh: 你要是现在不跟我走，我就狠狠揍你一顿。

segments.en: Well, Marco, in the dialogue, I heard one of the guys say, what's up?
segments.zh: 好吧，马可，在对话中，我听到其中一位人说，怎么了？

segments.en: But he said it in a really strange way, didn't he?
segments.zh: 但他说的很奇怪，不是吗？

segments.en: So in the 90s, it was popular instead of saying what's up, you would just kind of double the S and just say what's up.
segments.zh: 所以在 90 年代很流行，人们不直接说 what's up，而是把 S 拖长，说成 whassup。

segments.en: And then it became very famous with a TV commercial for a certain beer.
segments.zh: 然后它因某种啤酒的电视广告而变得非常有名。

segments.en: And actually, I remember this commercial during the Super Bowl.
segments.zh: 实际上，我记得在超级碗期间的这个广告。

segments.en: They had this big commercial where everyone was saying what's up in this really strange way, right?
segments.zh: 他们拍了这个大广告，每个人都用这种很奇怪的方式说 what's up，对吧？

segments.en: It's still used today informally between friends.
segments.zh: 它今天仍然在朋友之间非正式地使用。

segments.en: You'll go ahead, hey, what's up?
Yeah, so that commercial made it actually quite cool and famous to talk like that.
segments.zh: 是的，所以这个广告实际上让它变得很酷而且很有名。

segments.en: Actually in SpanishPod, they have a show called Que Pasa, which is like the translation of what's up.
segments.zh: 实际上，在 Spanishpod 中，他们有一个名为 Que Pasa 的节目，就像 What's Up 的翻译一样。

segments.en: They start each show with like saying, Que Pasa, but it's exactly the same.
segments.zh: 他们每期节目开头都说 Que Pasa，但这其实完全一样。

segments.en: So maybe it will become popular in Spanish.
segments.zh: 所以也许它会在西班牙语中流行起来。

segments.en: And as we heard typical music from the 90s.
segments.zh: 正如我们听到的 90 年代典型的音乐。

segments.en: And another interesting thing was the nicknames, Four Eyes, Mad Max, very popular among young kids.
segments.zh: 另一个有趣的事情是昵称，四眼，疯狂的麦克斯，在小孩中非常受欢迎。

segments.en: So remember, if you have any questions about this language or anything else about this lesson, come to our website at EnglishPod.com.
segments.zh: 所以请记住，如果您对这种语言或本课程有任何其他问题，请访问我们的网站 englishpod.com。

segments.en: You can leave all your questions and comments there and we hope to see you guys there.
segments.zh: 您可以将所有问题和评论留在那里，我们希望在那里见到你们。

segments.en: So thanks for listening and until next time.
segments.zh: 所以感谢您的收听，直到下一次。
